Find the derivative of the function using the definition of derivative. State the domain of the function and the domain of its derivative.

[;f(x) = mx + b;]

This question is intended as an example of how I think problems should be submitted. Please try to follow a similar formatting (although I won't be too strict). It's important to include the source information so that the problem can be searched for.

Given the function [;f(x) = mx + b;] and the definition of derivative [;f'(x) = \lim_{a \rightarrow 0} \frac{f(x+a)-f(x)}{a};],

[;f'(x) = \lim_{a \rightarrow 0} \frac{f(x+a)-f(x)}{a};]

[;f'(x) = \lim_{a \rightarrow 0} \frac{(m(x+a)+b)-(mx+b)}{a};]

[;f'(x) = \lim_{a \rightarrow 0} \frac{mx+ma+b-mx-b}{a};]

[;f'(x) = \lim_{a \rightarrow 0} \frac{mx+ma-mx}{a};]

[;f'(x) = \lim_{a \rightarrow 0} \frac{ma}{a};]

[;f'(x) = \lim_{a \rightarrow 0} m;]

[;f'(x) = m;]

The domain of the function [;f(x);], [;D = \{ x: x \epsilon \mathbb{R} \};].

The domain of its derivative [;f'(x) = m;], [;D = \{ x: x \epsilon \mathbb{R} \};].
